# Game pricing margin and inventory decisions — facts

> Source-anchored units about Game pricing margin and inventory decisions: 19 across 5 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 19 units · 5 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] A manufacturing-cost markup alone does not determine a viable game price. Looney Labs recommends comparing similar games by box size, perceived quality and complexity; Frank West explains that a five-times multiplier can produce an unworkable first-game MSRP when small-run costs are high. (medium confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-design-publishing · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] Mayday says it may buy some additional copies directly from the factory when a publisher increases a print run. Its claim that this can improve manufacturing economics is conditional on a buyer agreement; it does not establish savings for an uncommitted larger run. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.maydaygames.com/pages/board-game-publisher-overstock-program · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] The Game Crafter’s January 11, 2021 policy page describes its regular marketplace split as 70% of profit to the designer and 30% to the service. The percentages refer to profit, not to the full retail selling price; do not treat them as a universal distributor margin or a new negotiated quote. (low confidence) (verified as of 2021-01-11) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/124-70-30-profit-split · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions
- [statement] Mayday advertises purchasing selected excess game inventory for Mystery Boxes, but says it does not buy every title. It gives an indicative acquisition price around 90% off MSRP, with location-dependent variation. Treat this as one buyer’s contingent liquidation offer, not a guaranteed salvage value for unsold copies. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.maydaygames.com/pages/board-game-publisher-overstock-program · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions
- [statement] The Game Crafter’s ordinary marketplace documentation gives designers 70% of profit and the service 30%; its Sales page says it produces after a customer order and the designer remains responsible for promotion. This combines inventory exposure reduction with an ongoing demand-generation obligation. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2023-05-16) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/124-70-30-profit-split · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/131-sales

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Unsold games tie up cash: Stonemaier explains that retailers pay for stock before selling it, and Mayday describes recovering capital from slow-moving publisher inventory. A lower unit manufacturing cost therefore needs a separate assessment of cash committed to unsold copies. (medium confidence) — https://stonemaiergames.com/the-math-of-tariffs/ · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://www.maydaygames.com/pages/board-game-publisher-overstock-program
- [statement] The Game Crafter’s Crowd Sale FAQ requires family-friendly content and manual approval. Its Crowd Sale economics cannot be assumed available for every party-game design. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/401-crowd-sale-creator · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Looney Labs advises allowing for distributor discounts of at least 60% off MSRP; Frank West described a 60–65% discount in his March 2022 first-game pricing example. Treat these as attributed channel-planning benchmarks rather than a guaranteed contract for this game. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2022-03-08) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-design-publishing · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] The Game Crafter’s Bulk Pricing page, updated June 1, 2026, says discounts depend on the game components and some components retain fairly fixed costs at volume. Its bulk pricing counts complete games in one order, rather than sheets or components within one game; inspect the exact configured game instead of assuming a universal discount. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-06-01) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/84-bulk-pricing · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions
- [statement] Mayday’s overstock program is a limited salvage outlet, not assured full-price demand: it says typical purchases are 50–100 copies, reviews titles individually, and needs acquisition prices around 90% below MSRP, varying with location. This is Mayday’s commercial offer rather than an industry-wide liquidation rate. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.maydaygames.com/pages/board-game-publisher-overstock-program · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Direct sales can leave more revenue per copy, but the difference is not automatically net profit: Stonemaier includes publisher-paid warehousing and fulfillment, while Frank West identifies customer acquisition cost and shipping management as margin reductions. Compare channel contribution after these costs. (medium confidence) — https://stonemaiergames.com/the-math-of-tariffs/ · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] Separate per-copy contribution from business profit: Stonemaier says its simplified production-to-distributor spread excludes other costs, including freight, royalties and salaries; Frank West asks whether the remaining proceeds cover artwork, royalties, taxes and other expenses. (medium confidence) — https://stonemaiergames.com/the-math-of-tariffs/ · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] Looney Labs describes assessing distributor interest before deciding how many games to print, then taking distributor, retailer and consumer preorders. This is an operator example of using demand information to size inventory, not a demand forecast for a new party game. (low confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-design-publishing · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions
- [statement] The Game Crafter’s May 16, 2023 Sales page says it produces a game after a customer orders and ships to that customer; the creator remains responsible for promotion. Manufacturing after the order limits speculative finished-copy commitment in this marketplace workflow but does not establish demand. (low confidence) (verified as of 2023-05-16) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/131-sales · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions
- [statement] A unit-cost multiplier alone does not establish a viable game price: Looney Labs recommends comparison with similar games and accounting for personal time, while West tests whether remaining distributor-sale proceeds cover artwork, royalties, taxes and other expenses. (medium confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-design-publishing · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] Do not treat the manufacturing-to-sale spread as net profit. Stonemaier explicitly subtracts freight, salaries, royalties and sunk costs in its hypothetical example; West asks whether the remaining proceeds cover the creator’s expenses. (medium confidence) — https://stonemaiergames.com/the-math-of-tariffs/ · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] For direct sales, budget beyond production: Stonemaier identifies warehousing, fulfillment subsidies and possible discounts; West warns that customer acquisition can consume margin. These accounts do not establish a direct-sales margin for the commissioned game. (medium confidence) — https://stonemaiergames.com/the-math-of-tariffs/ · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://thecityofkings.com/news/how-to-price-your-game/
- [statement] The Game Crafter’s Crowd Sale FAQ documents a different payout arrangement from its ordinary marketplace split: it takes no percentage of Crowd Sale profit, and the designer chooses the per-copy payout. A margin model must distinguish these channels. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/401-crowd-sale-creator · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions · also: https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/124-70-30-profit-split
- [statement] In The Game Crafter’s Crowd Sale formula, the best bulk manufacturing cost plus designer profit determines the best sale price. Its FAQ says royalties become eligible only 30 days after sale and after shipment, so a booked sale is not immediate creator cash. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-11) — https://help.thegamecrafter.com/article/401-crowd-sale-creator · keywords: Game pricing margin and inventory decisions
